question: Where does the civilization information panel builder obtain and append each visible dynamic or fixed text field?

scope.boundary: This packet classifies the leader, civilization name, era-bonus block, normal trait text, Special Units heading, and Special Units values assembled by the supported civilization-selection builder. It does not classify other localization consumers or claim behavior outside this builder.

fields.stringLayout: The builder resolves the token value, scans the returned null-terminated string, and appends it through the existing string path.
The builder derives the civilization-indexed string address from r20, resolves the token value, scans the returned null-terminated string, and appends it through the existing string path.

fields.field: four era labels and four values
fields.kind: visible fixed labels and dynamic values after one hidden prefix
fields.stringLayout: An internal prefix plus four label/value pairs form a nine-line block. The separate owner-observed runtimeAcceptance records that the panel rendered only the eight label/value lines. The hook preserves the hidden prefix, can replace the four visible labels and values, and uses the string length stored at buffer address minus 4.

The producer call returns the localized trait buffer; the safe post-return hook boundary uses r30 for that string and r20 for the civilization selector. Its downstream layout carries the string length at buffer address minus 4.
The builder resolves the heading string and scans the returned null-terminated text before entering the unit loop.
At the unit value hook, r3 carries the localized value string, r27 carries the base unit type, and r20 carries the civilization selector before the builder appends the value and continues the loop.

fixedStrings.visibility: The owner-observed replacement result and non-rendered status for this stored line are recorded in runtimeAcceptance.

fixedStrings.layout: Together with the hidden prefix at 0x8212301C, this supplies the nine-line block consumed at 0x82D7807C.

currentEvidence.method: Foreground read-only Ghidra DumpFunctions and string-range queries against the supported image, with a narrow generated/default/rerevved_recomp.5.cpp comparison.

entries.role: normal trait producer and safe post-return hook
Special Units heading producer and hook boundary

currentEvidence.qualification: The Ghidra function view identifies the builder but decompiles it as a save/restore thunk; the narrow generated window supplies the producer sequence, hook boundaries, register dataflow, and buffer layout. The static locators establish producer mapping only; the separate owner-observed visible result is recorded in runtimeAcceptance.

runtimeAcceptance.enabledResult: The owner observed replacement leader, civilization, trait, four era labels, four era values, Special Units heading, and Keshik value in the civilization information panel.
runtimeAcceptance.hiddenPrefixResult: Replacing the internal Era Bonuses prefix produced no visible panel text.
runtimeAcceptance.qualification: This preserves the dated owner report; no exact tested-build identity or capture locator was retained with that report. It is not an independent replay and does not establish behavior for other localization consumers, language parity, multiplayer, or broader runtime coverage.

guards: Do not generalize these producer or hook boundaries to localization-global behavior beyond builder 0x82D77670.
Do not infer runtime reachability, final displayed values, language parity, or multiplayer behavior from this static mapping.
Preserve the hidden prefix, the eight visible era lines, and the length header at buffer address minus 4 when adapting the bounded hook.
Do not expose the internal Era Bonuses prefix as a visible presentation surface.
conclusion: The supported image's civilization information panel builder at 0x82D77670 has exact bounded text classifications: @RULER at 0x82D77F0C and @CIVNAME at 0x82D77FD0 both use civilization selector r20; the nine-line era block is hooked at 0x82D7807C, with a static layout consisting of the first Era Bonuses line followed by four label/value pairs; normal trait text is produced after 0x82D781A8 with a safe post-return hook at 0x82D781AC using r30/r20 and the minus-4 length header; the Special Units heading is produced at 0x82D78228; and each unit value reaches the hook at 0x82D783B4 with r3/r27/r20. The separate owner-observed runtimeAcceptance records that only the eight label/value lines were visible, along with the other listed replacements and no visible effect from replacing the first line.
